notable_absence.finding: The promoted index:memory-optimized-storage concept states plainly that memory-optimized storage is an Enterprise-Edition-only feature ('EE'). This page's own description of the 'memopt' value - 'To set the storage mode to use memory optimized indexes set this parameter to `memopt`.' - states no edition restriction whatsoever, unlike the concept it maps to. A reader relying solely on this CLI reference would not learn that --index-storage-setting memopt is unavailable on Community Edition.

cross_component_finding: This page's own text names the 'default' --index-storage-setting value as 'the disk based forestdb index backend' - a specific storage-engine name (Forestdb) that the promoted index:standard-storage concept's own description never uses (it says only 'CE default, disk-backed with supervisor process'), while the provided registry excerpt's index:index-storage-setting note describes the modern REST default as 'standard-storage (Plasma, default)'. Forestdb and Plasma are two different index storage engines - this CLI page's plain-language explanation of what 'default' means may describe an OLDER engine than the one the REST-facing standard-storage concept now defaults to, which is exactly the kind of staleness the round's authorship-provenance hypothesis (lighter TW review on engineer-owned CLI pages) predicts. This is worth a reconciliation-side check against the actual current default engine rather than taking either page's wording as settled.
cross_product_finding: The CLI's literal parameter values are terse two-word codes ('default', 'memopt') rather than the fuller descriptive names used elsewhere in the registry ('standard-storage', 'memory-optimized-storage') - a naming-register mismatch between this CLI surface and the REST-facing vocabulary, consistent with the round's CLI-vs-REST/UI terminology-drift watch item, though here the underlying meaning still lines up (registry_status promoted, not flagged as a conflict in identity - only in surface spelling).
